independence_day.intro: Ukraine’s Independence Day on 24 August marks the declaration of independence in 1991. It is an occasion to honour the country’s sovereignty, culture and people.
independence_day.history: On 24 August 1991, Ukraine’s parliament adopted the Act of Declaration of Independence. A nationwide referendum on 1 December confirmed the decision. Since Russia’s full-scale invasion in 2022, commemorations have also carried a strong message of resilience and remembrance.
independence_day.traditions: Blue-and-yellow flags and embroidered vyshyvanka shirts feature in celebrations. Communities organise cultural events, ceremonies and support for those affected by the war. Public gatherings depend on local conditions and security measures; Ukrainians abroad also mark the day.
funFacts: Ukraine celebrates National Flag Day on 23 August, the day before Independence Day.
The referendum confirming independence was held in December 1991.
Vyshyvanka embroidery patterns vary by region and tradition.
